subject: Re: DPA — training restrictions, response ownership & subprocessor map
messages:
From: Ellen Marsh <ellen.marsh@medisourcehealth.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com
Cc: David Chen <d.chen@medisourcehealth.com>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@procurex.co>
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA questions — treatment of LLM prompts/responses and transfer controls

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency profiles. The legal/procurement folks at MediSource have a couple of targeted DPA questions we need clarified before procurement can finish:

1) Training restriction: can you confirm whether data sent to the hosted API will ever be used to improve or retrain models? We need an explicit contractual commitment for any customers that mandate no-derivative/training use.

2) Response ownership and export controls: our deliverables team wants to ensure that generated outputs are not captured as IP by vendors and that exported results can be deleted on request.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: we require a current list of subprocessors, their locations, and whether any cross-border processing (EU/US) will occur for logs or KV caching. We also asked for an evidence packet about residency guarantees and logs retention.

I attached the draft DPA redlines from procurement for your legal review (see attachment). Can you route to the right folks and confirm whether Redwood can provide a clause for an explicit "training exclusion" and a simple mechanism to assert deletion and exportability of responses?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement has a hard internal deadline of 2/15.

Best,
Ellen Marsh
Head of Procurement — MediSource Health
ellen.marsh@medisourcehealth.com

Attachment: DPA_MediSource_v1_redlines.pdf (pdf)
From: aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com
To: Ellen Marsh <ellen.marsh@medisourcehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 14:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions — treatment of LLM prompts/responses and transfer controls

Ellen — thanks for sending this through and for the timeline. Looping in Ben (sales lead) and Priyom (privacy & compliance) so they can weigh in and propose language. Quick answers up front:

- Hosted API: by default we use telemetry/usage to improve model service quality, but we offer a binding Customer Data Setting (training_exclusion) for customers who require no-training commitments at the hosted tier. That setting is codified in the DPA addendum and can be applied per-account.

- Response ownership: customers retain rights to their prompts and outputs. We can add an export-and-delete workflow plus contract language that references data export formats and retention windows (logs vs. user payloads).

- Subprocessors: we maintain a current subprocessors matrix and service map. We'll provide the CSV and highlight any near-term changes. Cross-border handling depends on the routing policy — customers can pin region or require VPC/Private deployment for strict residency.

Priyom — can you review Ellen's redlines and propose suggested edits? Ben — I propose we offer a simple SOW add-on: training_exclusion clause + a 30-day evidence packet for subprocessor residency. Thoughts?

Cheers,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Aisha.Rahman@redwoodinference.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions — treatment of LLM prompts/responses and transfer controls

Aisha / team — reviewed the redlines and drafted proposed language. High-level points:

1) Training exclusion: we can commit to a contractual "Model Improvement Exclusion" that prohibits use of Customer Data (defined as prompts and customer payloads) for model training or improvement for customers that opt in. Implementation notes: apply a per-account flag that disables telemetry-based sampling and blocks retention of user payloads beyond ephemeral caching. We should add an exception carveout for severity-based safety improvements (security exploits) with strict minimization and notice.

Proposed DPA snippet (summary):
- "Customer Data shall not be used to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any models or model weights owned by Redwood Inference, unless Customer expressly authorizes such use in writing."

2) Response ownership & export: add clause that states "Customer retains exclusive rights to prompts and outputs; Redwood will provide data export in ndjson format within 10 business days of request and will delete residual payloads from production caches within 30 calendar days unless retention is required for security incident investigation."

3) Subprocessors & transfer evidence: we can attach our subprocessors matrix (CSV). For hosted customers selecting the training_exclusion, we will commit to providing a one-time residency attestation for logs and a 30-day notice for new subprocessors. For customers requiring strict residency, recommend Dedicated or Private deployment.

I attached the redlined DPA with inline suggestions and the subprocessors CSV. Happy to run through these with Ellen.

— Priyom
Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference
From: Ellen Marsh <ellen.marsh@medisourcehealth.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com
Cc: David Chen <d.chen@medisourcehealth.com>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@procurex.co>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions — treatment of LLM prompts/responses and transfer controls

Aisha / Priyom — thanks for the detailed draft language, that helps a lot. Procurement would accept the training exclusion snippet as long as there is:

- a clear definition of "Customer Data" that includes prompts and outputs (not aggregated telemetry)
- an auditable mechanism for verifying the account flag is in place (logs or attestation)
- a timeline for export and deletion that meets our legal standard (10 business days export, 30 days deletion is acceptable)

One follow-up on subprocessors: can you confirm whether any subprocessors process logs or KV cache in the EU and whether those records could be subject to cross-border transfer to the US for troubleshooting? We need that explicitly stated. Also, the security team will want a short notes pack describing how prefix/KV cache eviction is handled when training_exclusion is enabled.

If you can provide the attestation and the subprocessor statement by EOD Friday (2/13) we can keep to our procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Ellen
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Marsh <ellen.marsh@medisourcehealth.com>, aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions — treatment of LLM prompts/responses and transfer controls

Ellen — quick update from our side and commitments we can include in the DPA addendum: 

- Customer Data definition: we will add a clear definition that includes prompts, attachments submitted to the API, and generated outputs, and excludes aggregated telemetry.

- Account flag & attestation: for customers who opt into the "training_exclusion" we will provide an attestation document showing the exclusion flag is enabled and a short log excerpt demonstrating that post-flag requests are not stored beyond ephemeral cache. The attestation will be produced within 5 business days of contract signing.

- Subprocessors and cross-border handling: current subprocessors that handle logs are listed in the attached CSV. At present, logs/KV cache processing for EU-region customers is localized to EU subprocessors unless the customer selects a global routing policy. For troubleshooting cases that require cross-border escalation, we will: (a) require customer consent prior to any export of payloads; (b) restrict exports to masked/anonymized records where possible; (c) maintain an audit trail and notify the customer within 48 hours.

- Cache eviction: when training_exclusion is enabled, KV/prefix caches are configured to avoid persistent writes of user payloads. Ephemeral caches are evicted within 24 hours and a forced scrub process removes residual payloads from hot caches within 30 calendar days. We'll produce a short technical note describing the eviction and retention flow.

We can incorporate these commitments into the DPA addendum and the SOW — happy to share the redline and the attestation template. Would you like us to route the attestation through DocuSign?

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Sales Director — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
